first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it, so I gave it the first screen. It's calm and doesn't try to sell to me. 'We have been plain about which details come from UNESCO, the Smithsonian or parish sources and which are simply often told' is the sort of honesty I respect. It's a cultural guide, though, not a planner showing me what they can do. I read on because the family customs matter to my mother-in-law, not because it convinced me about the company.

journey.quote: We have followed them in the order families live them, and we have been plain about which details come from UNESCO, the Smithsonian or parish sources and which are simply often told.
journey.reaction: Understated and careful. No gushing. Good start.

journey.quote: treat what follows as a map to talk through with your parents and grandparents, not a rulebook.
journey.reaction: Right instinct. My family will have its own way of doing things and I don't want an outsider telling me what's 'correct'. They respect that.

journey.section: Lavash, honey and the broken plate at the door
journey.quote: For a wedding away from the family home, decide in advance where the "door" will be (a villa entrance, a ballroom foyer) and who will stand in the mother-in-law's place if she cannot travel.
journey.reaction: This is the first time it sounds like someone who has actually run one of these. Useful, practical detail I'd hand to my planner.

journey.quote: Leave the floor clear for a large group and warn the band it may run long.
journey.reaction: Fine, but 'a large group' for us means 300 people in the Kochari line. Nothing here shows they've handled numbers like that.

journey.quote: Dual Australian-Armenian nationals must enter and leave Armenia on their Armenian passport, and male dual nationals aged 18 to 28 may be liable for military service.
journey.reaction: Genuinely useful for a family with cousins who hold both passports. My assistant would note this one.

journey.quote: Plan the wedding, transfers and day trips well away from that band; a programme based in and around Yerevan keeps things simple.
journey.reaction: If we went to Armenia with several hundred guests, I'd want to hear about private transfers and security working with the venue's. 'Keeps things simple' is the only nod to logistics and it's not enough for me.

journey.quote: You will have a single point of contact, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins; the legal and church paperwork stays with you, the registry and your priest.
journey.reaction: Discreet, no price talk, no package language. I like a single point of contact. But it reads like it's aimed at a typical couple, not a family office.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland actually delivered an Armenian wedding, or any wedding of 200 to 400 guests?
Can they arrange exclusive use of a venue in or near Yerevan, and work alongside our own security team?
How do they handle privacy: guest phones, photographers, press?
Is there a private or referral route to them, rather than a general enquiry form?
would_share_with: My mother-in-law, for the sections on the asking, the kavor and the lavash
My assistant, for the dual-national passport and military service note

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like one person to coordinate the venue, travel and suppliers around those answers, speak with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: The tone is right and nothing cheapens it. But I enquire through referrals, and nothing on the page tells me they can handle our scale or keep things private. My assistant might click to see who's behind it; I wouldn't.

top_3_changes: In the Armenia destination section, add one understated line about what's possible for a large family wedding (exclusive use, private transfers, coordinating with a family's own security), only where it can be backed up.
Where the reception and Kochari are discussed, acknowledge very large guest numbers (hundreds, not dozens) so families like mine see themselves in it.
Give the closing CTA a quieter, private option (a direct conversation, not a form) for families who come through a referral.

checks.check: Every journey point and CTA reaction quotes the draft verbatim
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, Dubai, family office, discretion first)
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored as invisible
Absence of prices and deferred business details not treated as must-fix

open_questions.question: Persona is provisional and uncalibrated. Weight Layla's low enquiry score accordingly; this is a traditions guide where the UHNW persona is a secondary reader.

assumptions: Layla's assistant read first and summarised; Layla skimmed the intro, the doorway tip, the travel advice and the CTA.
An Armenian or Armenian-heritage family is relevant to her (in-laws), which makes the traditions content relevant.
